title: calloc failure check runs after pointer +1, so it never triggers
evidence: R_NewVisplane does `pl->top = (unsigned short*)calloc(...) + 1;` then `if (!pl->top || !pl->bottom) I_Error(...)`. A NULL calloc becomes (unsigned short*)2, non-NULL, so the check is dead; on OOM the next write to top[-1]/top[x] segfaults instead of the intended I_Error.
fix: Keep the raw calloc results in temporaries, check them, then add 1.
verified: If calloc returns NULL, adding 1 makes the pointer non-NULL, so the check at line 145 never fires; out-of-memory crashes instead of calling I_Error.

title: Looping MUS with no delay before scoreend spins forever in ProcessEvents
evidence: ProcessEvents (i_oplmus.c:713-812) loops `while (playing && delaytics == 0)`; on mus_scoreend with `looping` it calls Restart() and continues (783-788). A PWAD MUS whose events carry no delay (e.g. a score that is only a scoreend byte) never sets delaytics, so the loop never exits, inside the audio render path.
fix: Break out when a full pass from Restart reaches scoreend again without any delay having accumulated.
verified: Restart() sets delaytics=0 and the scoreend path skips the delay read, so a MUS lump with no delay before scoreend loops forever in ProcessEvents and hangs the game; needs a malformed lump.

title: Wall mesh is built once per level, so moving doors and lifts, switches and animated textures stay frozen
evidence: main.gd:33-38 calls level.build only when levelcount changes. DH_GetWalls (d_host.c) takes wall bounds from live sector heights and the sidedef textures. A door opening or a lift lowering changes those after the build, but the mesh keeps the original geometry. Switch texture swaps and wall animation don't show either. Floors and ceilings are listed as deliberately missing; moving walls aren't.
fix: Rebuild the wall mesh (or the affected walls) when sector heights or side textures change, or rebuild periodically.
verified: The only caller is main.gd:31 (level.build), once per level. Wall heights and textures are never refreshed after it, so moving doors and lifts, switches and animated textures stay frozen. The intent note excuses floors, ceilings, sky and masked textures, not this.

title: Textures with a non-power-of-two width tile with the wrong period in Godot
evidence: R_GetColumn masks col with texturewidthmask (the largest power of two at most the width, minus 1). DH_TextureRGBA bakes `width` columns, so columns past the mask repeat the early ones. level.gd and DH_GetWalls give u in texels divided by the full width, so Godot tiles with period `width`. The game tiles with period mask+1 (u & mask). For width 24, u=24 shows column 8 in the game but column 0 in Godot.
fix: Bake the image at the mask+1 width, or tell the host the tiling width and use it for u.
verified: R_GetColumn does col &= texturewidthmask[tex], the mask being the largest power of two at most the width, minus 1. For a width of 96, columns 64-95 hold columns 0-31, so the baked image repeats every 96 pixels in Godot while the game repeats every 64. A visual mismatch only.
